subject: Isolation footprint validation + procurement lane for HealthSpire regulated pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Alan Chu <alan.chu@healthspire.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@healthspire.com>
Date: 2026-08-08 09:12 -0700
Subject: Pilot hosting posture: numbers we need

Jonas — thanks for the call this morning. To move the pilot through security review we need a clear, itemized compute footprint and a short explanation of the failure/fallback modes. Specifically:
- Minimum on-prem hardware for an air-gapped pilot (PHI environment)
- If we choose Redwood Dedicated (reserved), what reserved pool sizing do you recommend for our expected workload (see below)?
- Network/egress assumptions and KMS approach for keys

Workload notes: 4 internal endpoints (clinical triage, patient summarization, billing assistance, chart search). Expected steady-state: ~4.5k requests/day with average prompt length ~450 tokens and generation avg 280 tokens. Peak concurrency observed in our mock traffic: ~95 concurrent active sessions.

We have a procurement review on Monday — can you send a short breakdown and call out any long lead items?

—Alan
Chief Clinical Officer, HealthSpire

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Dr. Alan Chu <alan.chu@healthspire.com>, Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@healthspire.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-08 13:47 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting posture: numbers we need

Alan — thanks, attached a compact sizing sheet and draft SOW (HealthSpire_SOW_v2.pdf and isolation-sizing-sheet.xlsx). High level summary below; see attachments for the per-model compute maps. TL;DR: recommend hybrid pilot (small on-prem air-gapped footprint + reserved Dedicated burst lane) to minimize risk while keeping predictable throughput and a fast path to scale.

Private (on-prem, air-gapped) pilot — minimal viable footprint:
- 4 x A100 80GB (or 2 x H100 80GB if procurement allows) in a single rack: supports model variants up to ~8B-13B quantized and handles local low-latency inference for PHI data.
- Local inference node config: 2x CPU sockets, 512GB RAM, NVMe cache for model shards, 10Gbps internal network.
- Ops ask: one systems engineer on-site for install + KMS network breakout for 1 week.
- Pros: full data custody, easiest to satisfy strict air-gap controls.
- Cons: limited burst capacity and slower model iteration cadence (we will push optimized kernels remotely where possible).

Dedicated (Redwood reserved pool) — recommended reserved slate for pilot and first 6 months:
- Reserved: 12 x A100 80GB (reserved pool in us-west) with burst allowance to 24 x A100 for spikes. That sizing targets sustained throughput for ~95 concurrency with headroom for 2x traffic growth and model A/B testing of 2 variants.
- Routing: PHI traffic pinned to Private nodes; de-identified/ancillary traffic can route to Dedicated with strict routing policy.
- Fallback: when Dedicated capacity is saturated, requests fall back to quantized model variants (3-bit) with slightly degraded quality or queue with SLA-based soft-throttling.

Estimated economics (very rough):
- One-time on-prem setup + install: ~$45k (hardware amortized, install labor).
- Monthly reserved Dedicated cost (12 x A100 reserved, with support): ~$85k/mo (we will provide exact quote from finance).

Procurement notes / long lead items:
- H100 procurement lead time (if chosen) can be 8–12 weeks.
- SOC 2 and KMS integration details (we have a standard ATO packet) — see SOW appendix.

Next steps: I suggest a short call with procurement tomorrow to confirm timeline and DocuSign path. Marissa / Karthik — can you confirm the finance quote and add any contractual items we should surface to HealthSpire procurement?

—Jonas
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Alan Chu <alan.chu@healthspire.com>, HealthSpire Procurement <procurement@healthspire.com>
Date: 2026-08-09 08:30 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting posture: numbers we need

Looping in finance + procurement counsel. Quick clarifications and asks: 
- We should offer two commercial lanes in the SOW: (A) Pilot reserved (12 A100) with a 3-month opt-out and (B) Pilot hybrid (4 on-prem + 6 reserved) with slightly lower monthly commitment. This gives HealthSpire flexibility and helps close faster.
- Add explicit SLA floor for model availability (99.5% for Dedicated; Private uptime depends on customer infra but we will include best-effort support + runbook).
- For the quote: I will get exact list pricing and a markdown for pilot commits; Karthik, please confirm discount tier for regulated pilots.

Karthik — any constraints on the KMS/HSM integration we should call out? They asked for in-country key custody, which is fine for the US. We should specify recommended KMS providers in the appendix (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS + customer-managed keys).

—Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Alan Chu <alan.chu@healthspire.com>, HealthSpire Procurement <procurement@healthspire.com>
Date: 2026-08-09 10:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting posture: numbers we need

Agree with Marissa. Couple of technical & procurement points to surface explicitly in the SOW and procurement packet: 
1) Capacity tiling: propose a runway plan — Month 0 (pilot): hybrid 4 on-prem + 6 reserved; Month 1–3: 12 reserved; Month 4+: scale to 24 reserved if traffic growth >60%. Include a readout cadence (weekly for first month, then bi-weekly).
2) Model variants and quantization: call out which models will be certified for PHI (we'll propose 7B quantized, 13B quantized, and a fall-back 70B trimmed-llama variant only in Dedicated non-PHI lanes).
3) Break-glass plan: if on-prem node fails, we fallback to Dedicated with an encrypted VPN tunnel and a documented approval flow — this requires signed acceptance in the SOW.
4) Lead times: hardware and procurement approvals are the blocker. If HealthSpire can accept A100s instead of H100s we can shorten procurement by ~6 weeks.

I'll attach a short procurement checklist to the DocuSign package.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: HealthSpire Procurement <procurement@healthspire.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Dr. Alan Chu <alan.chu@healthspire.com>, Rachel Lin <rachel.lin@healthspire.com>
Date: 2026-08-10 16:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot hosting posture: numbers we need

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement timeline: we need a formal quote + finalized SOW and will aim to route to our legal + security committee by Aug 18. A few clarifying questions before we escalate: 
- Can you confirm that the on-prem footprint (4 x A100 80GB) will be fully air-gapped during normal operations, and define the maintenance window/process for software updates?
- Please include a short privacy/data flow diagram in the appendix (where PHI stays, where de-identified traffic may go).
- Who is the Redwood on-call for the pilot (name + escalation number) during the first 90 days?

If you can send a DocuSign SOW and a quote by EOD tomorrow we should be able to make the Aug 18 committee.

—Procurement Team
HealthSpire
